writes.rule: Per subtopic seen: pMastery 0.7 if right at D2/D3, 0.55 if right at D1, 0.25 if wrong; level L0-L3 from the ladder step reached
Prerequisite-gap index = 100 x weighted misses / weighted items seen in slots 1-4, averaged over groups
Groups with the highest Part A percent (top 1-2, only if >= 65%)
Groups with the lowest Part A percent (bottom 1-2, only if < 65%)
Calibration = 1 - mean |confidence/5 - correct| over Part A (feeds the first MCI reading)
Highest difficulty answered correctly twice in a row: D1 low, D2 medium, D3 high
Verbal reasoning = percent of Part B verbal items right
Numerical reasoning = percent of Part B numerical items right
Abstract reasoning = percent of Part B abstract items right
Spatial reasoning = percent of Part B spatial items right
Logical deduction = percent right on Part B items tagged p65
Numeracy fluency = numerical percent scaled by speed (right answers under target time count 1.2x, max 100)
Processing speed = 100 x share of Part B items answered right within target seconds
RIASEC profile: each career-interest item scored 1-5; letter score = mean of its 2 items; top 3 letters form the code (e.g. IRC)

items.markingKey: B. (-5, 0). Points on the x-axis have y = 0

items.subtopicHint: Distance between two points using the Baudhayana-Pythagoras theorem

items.subtopicHint: Distance between two points using the Baudhayana-Pythagoras theorem
items.markingKey: C. Yes, and BC = 5. The angle at A is 90°; BC = √(16 + 9) = 5

items.stem: Which of these is a linear polynomial?
items.markingKey: C. 3x + 2. The highest power of x is 1

items.stem: What is the zero of p(x) = 2x - 6?
items.markingKey: B. 3. 2x - 6 = 0 gives x = 3

items.markingKey: C. √5. √16 = 4; 22/7 is a fraction

items.stem: The decimal expansion of an irrational number is
items.markingKey: C. non-terminating and non-recurring. Recurring decimals are rational

items.stem: Which of these numbers is rational?
items.markingKey: D. (3 + √2) - √2. The √2 terms cancel, leaving 3

items.stem: Why does the smell of perfume spread across a still room?
items.answer: Its particles diffuse, moving randomly from high to low concentration
options: Air pushes the perfume in one direction
Its particles diffuse, moving randomly from high to low concentration
Perfume is lighter than air, so it only rises
items.markingKey: C. Its particles diffuse, moving randomly from high to low concentration. Random particle motion spreads the perfume out

items.stem: Which of these is a compound?
items.markingKey: A. water. Water is hydrogen and oxygen chemically joined; air is a mixture

items.stem: Which statement about a mixture of iron filings and sulfur powder is true?
items.answer: The iron can be separated with a magnet
options: The iron can be separated with a magnet
items.markingKey: C. The iron can be separated with a magnet. In a mixture each substance keeps its own properties

items.stem: Pressure is
items.subtopicHint: Pressure as force per unit area
items.markingKey: B. force per unit area. p = F / A

items.stem: Why is it easier to cut with a sharp knife than a blunt one?
items.answer: The sharp edge has a smaller area, so the same force gives more pressure
items.subtopicHint: Pressure as force per unit area
options: Blunt knives only have more friction
Sharp knives push with more force by themselves
The sharp edge has a smaller area, so the same force gives more pressure
items.markingKey: D. The sharp edge has a smaller area, so the same force gives more pressure. Smaller area, larger pressure

items.stem: A box weighing 600 N rests on a base of area 0.5 m². What pressure does it exert on the floor?
items.subtopicHint: Pressure as force per unit area

items.stem: Which part of a cell controls its activities?
items.subtopicHint: Cell structure: plant and animal cells
items.markingKey: D. nucleus. The nucleus holds the genetic instructions

items.stem: Onion peel cells and cheek cells are viewed under a microscope. Which difference will you see?
items.answer: Onion cells have a cell wall and a regular shape; cheek cells do not
items.subtopicHint: Cell structure: plant and animal cells
options: Cheek cells have a large central vacuole
Onion cells have a cell wall and a regular shape; cheek cells do not
items.markingKey: D. Onion cells have a cell wall and a regular shape; cheek cells do not. Only plant cells have cell walls

items.stem: A cell placed in pure water swells but does not burst. Which cell is it most likely to be?
items.answer: A plant cell, because its cell wall resists bursting
items.subtopicHint: Cell structure: plant and animal cells
options: A plant cell, because its cell wall resists bursting
Any cell, since water never enters cells
An animal cell, because it has a cell membrane
items.markingKey: A. A plant cell, because its cell wall resists bursting. Animal cells without a wall can burst in pure water

items.stem: Which organelle is called the 'powerhouse of the cell'?
items.markingKey: B. mitochondria. Mitochondria release energy as ATP

items.stem: Lysosomes are called 'suicide bags' because
items.answer: their enzymes can digest the cell's own parts if the cell is damaged
options: their enzymes can digest the cell's own parts if the cell is damaged
items.markingKey: B. their enzymes can digest the cell's own parts if the cell is damaged. Lysosomes hold digestive enzymes

items.stem: Cells of a gland that secretes large amounts of protein are likely to have many
items.answer: ribosomes and a well-developed ER and Golgi apparatus
options: ribosomes and a well-developed ER and Golgi apparatus
items.markingKey: C. ribosomes and a well-developed ER and Golgi apparatus. Proteins are made on ribosomes and packaged by the ER and Golgi

items.stem: Movement of water across a selectively permeable membrane from a dilute to a concentrated solution is called
items.markingKey: B. osmosis. Osmosis is the diffusion of water across a membrane

items.stem: Raisins left in water swell up because
items.markingKey: D. water enters them by osmosis. The raisin cells are more concentrated than water

items.stem: Salt sprinkled on cucumber slices makes drops of water appear on them. Explain why.
items.answer: Water moves out of the cells by osmosis into the more concentrated salt solution
options: Cucumber cells make water when salted
Water moves out of the cells by osmosis into the more concentrated salt solution
items.markingKey: B. Water moves out of the cells by osmosis into the more concentrated salt solution. Water moves from dilute (cell sap) to concentrated (salt)

items.stem: Displacement is different from distance because displacement
items.markingKey: A. has a direction. Displacement is a vector

items.stem: A runner completes one full lap of a 400 m track in 80 s. What are her average speed and displacement?
items.markingKey: A. 5 m/s and 0 m. She ends where she started

items.stem: A car travels 30 km at 60 km/h and then 30 km at 30 km/h. What is its average speed for the whole trip?
items.markingKey: C. 40 km/h. Total 60 km in 0.5 h + 1 h = 1.5 h

items.stem: A car speeds up from rest to 20 m/s in 5 s. What is its acceleration?
items.subtopicHint: Acceleration and the equations of motion

items.stem: A bus moving at 15 m/s brakes with a uniform retardation of 3 m/s². How long does it take to stop?
items.subtopicHint: Acceleration and the equations of motion

items.stem: A ball is dropped from rest and falls 20 m (take a = 10 m/s²). Using v² = u² + 2as, how fast is it moving just before it lands?
items.subtopicHint: Acceleration and the equations of motion

items.stem: The ground is wet and people are carrying umbrellas. It ___ have rained.
items.markingKey: C. must. 'Must have' expresses a confident deduction

items.stem: Which sentence is punctuated correctly as direct speech?
items.markingKey: B. "Close the window," said Mother.. Only the spoken words go inside the quotation marks, followed by a comma

items.stem: Change to indirect speech: She said, 'I will call you tomorrow.'
items.answer: She said that she would call me the next day.
options: She said she will called me tomorrow.
She said that she would call me the next day.
She told that she would calls me the next day.
She said that I will call you tomorrow.
items.markingKey: B. She said that she would call me the next day.. 'Will' becomes 'would', 'tomorrow' becomes 'the next day'

items.stem: Which is the best title for a paragraph about saving water by fixing leaks, using buckets and reusing water?
items.markingKey: A. Simple Ways to Save Water. A title should cover the main idea of the whole paragraph

items.stem: Read: "Mangroves grow along tropical coasts. Their tangled roots hold soil in place, slow down storm waves and shelter young fish. Many mangrove forests are being cleared for farms and buildings." Which summary is best?
items.answer: Mangroves protect coasts and wildlife but are being cleared
options: Farms are more important than mangroves
Mangroves protect coasts and wildlife but are being cleared
items.markingKey: D. Mangroves protect coasts and wildlife but are being cleared. A summary keeps the main points and leaves out detail

items.stem: Which sentence would NOT belong in a summary of a text explaining how vaccines work?
items.answer: My cousin was scared of injections when he was little.
options: My cousin was scared of injections when he was little.
Vaccines train the immune system to recognise germs.
This prepares the body to fight infection quickly.
items.markingKey: A. My cousin was scared of injections when he was little.. Personal anecdotes are not main points

items.stem: 'Silent sea, softly sighing' mainly uses
items.markingKey: C. alliteration. The repeated 's' sound

items.stem: 'I have told you a million times!' is an example of
items.markingKey: D. hyperbole. Deliberate exaggeration for effect

items.stem: What is the effect of the simile in 'Her words were as sharp as broken glass'?
items.answer: It shows her words were hurtful
options: It shows her words were hurtful
items.markingKey: D. It shows her words were hurtful. Broken glass cuts, so the words wounded

items.stem: Read: "Krishtakka, the narrator's grandmother, could not read. Each week she waited for her granddaughter to read the next part of a serialised novel aloud. When the girl went away for a few days, Krishtakka decided to learn to read herself." Why did she decide to learn?
items.answer: She could not follow the story while her granddaughter was away
items.subtopicHint: How I Taught My Grandmother to Read: literacy and determination
options: She wanted to become a writer
She needed to read bus timetables
She could not follow the story while her granddaughter was away
items.markingKey: D. She could not follow the story while her granddaughter was away. Her dependence on the granddaughter became a problem when the girl left

items.stem: Read: "Krishtakka, the narrator's grandmother, could not read. When her granddaughter went away for a few days, she decided to learn to read herself, and asked the girl to teach her." What does this show about her?
items.answer: Determination: she believed it was never too late to learn
items.subtopicHint: How I Taught My Grandmother to Read: literacy and determination
options: Determination: she believed it was never too late to learn
items.markingKey: C. Determination: she believed it was never too late to learn. An elderly learner choosing to start shows resolve

items.stem: In the story, the granddaughter becomes her grandmother's teacher. What is the effect of this role reversal?
items.answer: It shows learning can flow from young to old and challenges the usual roles
items.subtopicHint: How I Taught My Grandmother to Read: literacy and determination
options: It only makes the story funny
It shows children are always wiser
It shows the grandmother could not learn
It shows learning can flow from young to old and challenges the usual roles
items.markingKey: D. It shows learning can flow from young to old and challenges the usual roles. The reversal carries the theme of respect for learning at any age

items.stem: Choose the correct word: She said that she ___ tired.
items.markingKey: C. was. A past reporting verb takes a past tense in the reported clause

items.stem: Choose the correct words: If it rains tomorrow, we ___ the match.
items.markingKey: C. will postpone. First conditional: if + present, will + verb

items.stem: Which sentence is correct?
items.answer: He told me that he had finished his homework before dinner.
options: He told me that he had finished his homework before dinner.
He told me that he has finished his homework before dinner.
He told me that he will finished his homework before dinner.
He told me that he finish his homework before dinner.
items.markingKey: A. He told me that he had finished his homework before dinner.. An earlier past action takes the past perfect

items.stem: 'O mighty river, carry my song!' Speaking directly to a river is an example of
items.subtopicHint: Bharat Our Land: personification, alliteration and apostrophe
items.markingKey: B. apostrophe. Apostrophe addresses something absent or non-human

items.stem: Which line contains personification?
items.answer: The mountains stand guard over the sleeping valley.
items.subtopicHint: Bharat Our Land: personification, alliteration and apostrophe
options: The mountains stand guard over the sleeping valley.
The river is like a ribbon.
items.markingKey: A. The mountains stand guard over the sleeping valley.. Standing guard and sleeping are human actions

items.stem: Why might a patriotic poem describe the land as a 'mother'?
items.answer: To suggest love, care and a bond of belonging between the people and the land
items.subtopicHint: Bharat Our Land: personification, alliteration and apostrophe
options: To show the land is old
To suggest love, care and a bond of belonging between the people and the land
Because the poet's mother lived there
items.markingKey: B. To suggest love, care and a bond of belonging between the people and the land. The metaphor carries emotional meaning

items.stem: You ___ wear a helmet while riding a scooter; it is the law.
items.markingKey: D. must. 'Must' expresses obligation

items.stem: ___ I borrow your pen, please?
items.markingKey: B. May. 'May' asks politely for permission

items.stem: Which sentence expresses a strong deduction?
items.answer: She must be at home; her bicycle is outside.
options: She must be at home; her bicycle is outside.
items.markingKey: D. She must be at home; her bicycle is outside.. 'Must be' draws a confident conclusion from evidence

items.stem: Members of the Lok Sabha are
items.subtopicHint: Parliament: Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha
items.markingKey: D. directly elected by the people. Rajya Sabha members are elected by state legislatures

items.stem: The Revolt of 1857 began among sepoys at
items.markingKey: D. Meerut. It started on 10 May 1857

items.answer: Rumours that new rifle cartridges were greased with cow and pig fat
options: Rumours that new rifle cartridges were greased with cow and pig fat

items.stem: Who led the Dandi March (Salt Satyagraha) in 1930?
items.markingKey: C. Mahatma Gandhi. Gandhi walked from Sabarmati to Dandi

items.stem: The Quit India Movement was launched in
items.markingKey: D. 1942. Launched in August 1942

items.stem: Why did Gandhi choose salt as the focus of a protest?
items.answer: Everyone used salt, so the salt tax hurt rich and poor alike and united people
options: Everyone used salt, so the salt tax hurt rich and poor alike and united people
The British had banned eating salt
items.markingKey: C. Everyone used salt, so the salt tax hurt rich and poor alike and united people. A universal grievance built mass participation

items.stem: Which of these is a factor of production?
items.markingKey: A. Labour. Land, labour, capital and entrepreneurship

items.stem: A farmer's tractor is an example of
items.markingKey: C. capital. Capital is human-made equipment

items.stem: Why does better education and health raise a country's production?
items.answer: It increases human capital: skilled, healthy workers produce more
options: It increases the amount of land
It increases human capital: skilled, healthy workers produce more
It reduces the number of workers
items.markingKey: B. It increases human capital: skilled, healthy workers produce more. Human capital is productive

items.stem: Which is a primary source for studying the Harappan civilisation?
items.subtopicHint: Sources and evidence in social science
items.markingKey: C. Seals excavated at Mohenjo-daro. Primary sources come from the period itself

items.stem: Why do social scientists use more than one source?
items.answer: To cross-check facts and reduce bias
items.subtopicHint: Sources and evidence in social science
options: Because one source is not allowed
To cross-check facts and reduce bias
items.markingKey: B. To cross-check facts and reduce bias. Corroboration strengthens conclusions

items.stem: A survey of only city residents is used to describe farmers' incomes. What is the main problem?
items.answer: The sample does not represent the group being studied
items.subtopicHint: Sources and evidence in social science
options: The sample does not represent the group being studied
items.markingKey: D. The sample does not represent the group being studied. Conclusions need a representative sample

items.stem: Most earthquakes occur

items.stem: The Himalayas were formed by
items.answer: the collision of the Indian plate with the Eurasian plate
items.subtopicHint: Plate tectonics: earthquakes and mountain building
options: the collision of the Indian plate with the Eurasian plate
items.markingKey: B. the collision of the Indian plate with the Eurasian plate. They are young fold mountains

items.stem: Why is the Himalayan region still prone to earthquakes?
items.answer: The Indian plate is still pushing into the Eurasian plate
items.subtopicHint: Plate tectonics: earthquakes and mountain building
options: The Indian plate is still pushing into the Eurasian plate
items.markingKey: A. The Indian plate is still pushing into the Eurasian plate. Ongoing collision builds stress

items.stem: The south-west monsoon brings most of India's rain during
items.markingKey: D. June to September. This is the rainy season

items.stem: Why does Mawsynram in Meghalaya receive very heavy rainfall?
items.answer: Moist winds from the Bay of Bengal are forced to rise over the Khasi Hills
options: Moist winds from the Bay of Bengal are forced to rise over the Khasi Hills
items.markingKey: A. Moist winds from the Bay of Bengal are forced to rise over the Khasi Hills. Rising air cools and releases rain (relief rainfall)

items.stem: Why does Tamil Nadu receive much of its rain in October and November?
items.answer: The retreating north-east monsoon picks up moisture over the Bay of Bengal
options: It is shielded from all monsoon winds
The south-west monsoon is strongest then
The retreating north-east monsoon picks up moisture over the Bay of Bengal
items.markingKey: C. The retreating north-east monsoon picks up moisture over the Bay of Bengal. The Tamil Nadu coast lies in the rain shadow of the south-west monsoon

items.stem: Which Harappan city had the Great Bath?
items.subtopicHint: Harappan Civilisation: cities, economy and trade
items.markingKey: A. Mohenjo-daro. It is in present-day Sindh

items.stem: Lothal was an important Harappan site because it had
items.subtopicHint: Harappan Civilisation: cities, economy and trade
items.markingKey: C. a dockyard used for trade. Lothal in Gujarat was a port

items.stem: Which evidence suggests that Harappan cities were planned?
items.answer: Streets laid out in a grid and covered drains
items.subtopicHint: Harappan Civilisation: cities, economy and trade
options: Streets laid out in a grid and covered drains
items.markingKey: D. Streets laid out in a grid and covered drains. Town planning shows central organisation
